issue.title: just check fails at lint (patch/stitch terminology): sase-core at_bearing_notes fixture flagged as defect
issue.description:
## CI failure

- **Node:** `lint (patch/stitch terminology)` — `tools/audit_patch_stitch_terminology --repo-root . --allow-missing-linked-repos` via `just check` recipe `_lint-patch-stitch-terminology`

`just check` fails at the patch/stitch terminology lint on a clean tree. All 14 reported defects are historical note bodies inside the linked sase-core fixture `crates/sase_core/tests/fixtures/note_attachment/at_bearing_notes.jsonl` (lines 338, 412, 494, 574, 690, 709, 713, 724, 725, 915 — each counted twice for `ChangeSpec`/`changespec` token variants). They are restored 2026-07 memory-episode notes whose prose mentions "ChangeSpec COMMITS refs", "agents/changespecs/axe", etc. Zero defects are reported in the main repo. The fixture path suggests these should fall under the audit's `legacy-data-test-fixture` retained-token class rather than `defect (unclassified)`, or the fixture needs an explicit allowlist entry — the worker should decide which.

Why this is not a flake: the audit is deterministic over file contents. Reproduced identically (14 defects, exit 1) with the reporter's unrelated working-tree changes stashed, i.e. on the untouched base tree, and the offending file is not touched by that work. Evidence: monitor zj4rtz2k29t5 (`sase tool show 771fb9eeefc119adda5f130c268895a0`).

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic content audit, not a test-order or timing issue: identical 14 defects and exit 1 with the reporter's changes stashed (untouched base tree), and all defects are in sase-core fixture file at_bearing_notes.jsonl which that work does not touch.

issue.creation_reason: just check cannot pass on a clean tree because the terminology audit flags historical fixture text in the linked sase-core repo; filing so the pre-existing failure is tracked separately from the xprompt string-defaults work.
